summary: Freedom of speech, religion, press, assembly, and petition.
Right to keep and bear arms.
No quartering of soldiers in private homes without consent.
Protection from unreasonable search and seizure.
Right to due process, no double jeopardy, no self-incrimination.
Right to a speedy, public trial by an impartial jury and to legal counsel.
Right to a jury trial in civil cases.
No excessive bail or fines, no cruel and unusual punishment.
Rights not listed in the Constitution are still retained by the people.
Powers not given to the federal government belong to the states or the people.
Limits lawsuits against states by citizens of another state or country.
Revised presidential election procedure — separate ballots for President and VP.
Abolished slavery.
Citizenship and equal protection under the law for all persons born or naturalized in the U.S.
Right to vote cannot be denied based on race, color, or previous servitude.
Authorizes a federal income tax.
Direct election of U.S. Senators by popular vote.
Prohibited the manufacture, sale, and transport of alcohol (repealed by the 21st).
Women's right to vote.
Moved presidential/congressional term start dates ('Lame Duck' Amendment).
Repealed Prohibition (the 18th Amendment).
Limits the President to two elected terms.
Grants Washington, D.C. electoral votes for President.
Banned poll taxes in federal elections.
Presidential succession and disability procedures.
Lowered the voting age to 18.
Congressional pay raises take effect only after the next election.
